chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one he mentioned, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

You will not be righteous until you know, and you will not know until you ratify, and you will not ratify until you submit to four doors — the first of which is not correct except with its last. They strayed, the companions of the three, wandering in a far wandering.

Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, accepts nothing except righteous deeds, and Allah accepts nothing except fulfilment of the stipulations and covenants. So whoever fulfils Allah's, Mighty and Majestic's, stipulation and acts according to what is described in His covenant, shall attain what is with Him and complete what He promised.
Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, informed the servants of the paths of guidance and established for them therein the beacons, and informed them how they should travel.
So He said: "And I am indeed Most Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds, then follows the right guidance." [20:82]

And He said: "Allah only accepts from the God-fearing." [5:27] So whoever fears Allah with regard to what He commanded him, shall meet Allah as a believer in what Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) brought.

Alas! Alas! A people passed away and died before being guided, and they thought they had believed, yet they had committed shirk from an aspect they did not perceive. Verily, whoever comes to the houses through their doors is guided, and whoever takes another path has walked the road of ruin.

Allah has linked obedience to the guardian of His command with obedience to His Messenger, and obedience to His Messenger with obedience to Himself. So whoever abandons obedience to the masters of authority has obeyed neither Allah nor His Messenger — and this is the acknowledgement of what was revealed from the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
"Take your adornment at every mosque," [7:31] and seek the houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted and His name to be mentioned in them. [24:36]

For He informed you that they are "men whom neither commerce nor sale diverts from the remembrance of Allah and the keeping up of prayer and the giving of zakat — they fear a day in which the hearts and eyes shall be overturned." [24:37]
Indeed Allah had selected the Messengers for His command, then selected them as ratifiers with that in His warners.
So He said: "And there is not a people but a warner has gone among them." [35:24]
He strayed who was ignorant, and he was guided who had insight and intellect.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "For surely it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are in the chests." [22:46]
And how can he be guided who lacks insight, and how can he have insight who does not reflect?

Follow the Messenger of Allah and the People of his Household, and acknowledge what was revealed from the presence of Allah, and follow the traditions of guidance — for they are the signs of faithfulness and piety. Know that if a man were to deny Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon her) while accepting all other Messengers, he would not be a believer. Navigate the road by seeking the beacons, and seek from behind the veils the traditions — you will complete the matter of your religion and become believers in Allah, your Lord.

key_terms.أَبْوَاباً أَرْبَعَةً: Four doors/gates — the four fundamental conditions of righteous faith in Shia theology
key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الثَّلَاثَةِ: Companions of the three — those who accepted only three of the four conditions, likely referring to those who accepted the first three caliphs but not Imam Ali
key_terms.الْآثَارُ: Traditions/signs — the Imams' teachings and hadiths as signs of guidance
key_terms.الْحُجُبُ: Veils/screens — the barriers between the seeker and the truth
key_terms.الْمَنَارَ: Beacons/lighthouses — metaphor for the Imams as guides on the path of guidance
key_terms.تَعْرِفُوا: Recognition/knowledge (ma'rifa) — specifically knowledge/recognition of the Imam
key_terms.تُسَلِّمُوا: Submission/surrender — complete submission to the Imam's guidance
key_terms.تُصَدِّقُوا: Ratification/affirmation — affirming the Imam's authority and teachings
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْأَمْرِ: The guardian/master of the command — the rightful Imam

ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions of righteousness according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a comprehensive doctrinal sermon on the four conditions of becoming truly righteous: recognition of the Imam (ma'rifa), ratification (tasdiq), submission (taslim), and their interdependence. The hadith was directed at Shia Muslims who may have accepted some but not all four pillars of the faith, warning that partial acceptance — like accepting three of the four — leads to irredeemable misguidance. The Imam grounds his argument in multiple Quranic verses, demonstrating that obedience to the waliy al-amr (the guardian of authority) is Quranically mandated and inseparable from obedience to God and the Prophet.
